Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Fever for ~7 days with intermittent hot sweats and night sweats.
  - Generalized myalgia (aching all over).
  - Nausea with reduced oral intake and decreased fluid intake.
  - Fatigue and malaise limiting ability to work.
  - Recent travel to Vietnam; returned 4 weeks ago with rural exposure (trekking, cycling through farmland).
  - Took malaria prophylaxis while overseas (patient cannot recall medication name; reports daily dosing and possibly an additional medication on top of the first — name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Has chronic back pain (under physiotherapy; attributed to prolonged sitting/posture).

- Relevant family medical history:
  - Father died of a myocardial infarction in his late 60s (reported age ~68).

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  - Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Paracetamol (OTC; patient reports taking recommended dose daily — dose/route/frequency not fully documented).
  - Ibuprofen (OTC; patient reports taking recommended dose daily — dose/route/frequency not fully documented).
  - Malaria prophylaxis taken while travelling (name/dose/route/frequency not documented; patient reports daily and an additional medication taken on top).

- Immunisation status reviewed:
  - Patient reports being up to date with vaccinations, including hepatitis B.

- Sexual and reproductive health:
  - Not recorded.

- Physical activity and nutrition:
  - Normally performs moderate physical exercise a few times per week.
  - Currently reduced appetite and lower fluid intake due to nausea.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  - Non-smoker.
  - Reports moderate alcohol intake (quantity/frequency not documented).
  - No other substance use documented.

- Hearing loss or concerns:
  - Denies ear pain or hearing problems.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):
  - On Seroxat (medication implies previous/ongoing mental health treatment; diagnosis not documented).
  - Reports feeling significantly tired and struggling at work.
  - No screening for depression, self-harm, or suicidal ideation documented.

- Vision problems or recent changes:
  - Reports chronic headaches related to screen use; no new visual changes documented.

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  - Employed as a nurse.
  - Under physiotherapy for back pain.
  - No caring responsibilities documented.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:
  - Not recorded.

- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):
  - Not recorded.

- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):
  - Not recorded.

- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):
  - Not recorded (patient denies ear symptoms).

- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):
  - Not recorded.

- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):
  - Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):
  - Not recorded / not indicated in transcript.

- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):
  - Not recorded.

- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):
  - Not recorded.

- Mammogram (if eligible):
  - Not recorded.

- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):
  - Planned/requested investigations from clinician:
    - Thick and thin blood films for malaria.
    - Inflammatory markers and other blood tests (specific panels not fully detailed in transcript).
  - Urgency of tests to be determined after in-clinic physical examination.

Management Plan

- Summary of key management actions and recommendations:
  - Patient advised to attend an in-person clinic appointment (central London) for clinical examination and to determine urgency of blood tests.
  - If clinic attendance is inconvenient, patient advised she may attend local Emergency Department; clinician will document the suggested tests in the notes for presentation to reception/ED.
  - Requested investigations: thick and thin blood films (for malaria), inflammatory markers, and additional blood tests as determined by examining clinician.
  - Advised patient not to work until the cause of fever is clarified.
  - Administrative action: clinician will ask admin team to book an urgent clinic appointment; patient instructed to phone the provided number in consultation notes to be slotted in.
  - No immediate prescription or additional interventions documented beyond continuing OTC paracetamol/ibuprofen taken by patient.

- Referrals / follow-up:
  - Urgent GP clinic (or A&E) assessment for examination and blood tests to be arranged.
  - Physiotherapy ongoing for chronic back pain (already in place).
  - No other referrals (mental health, allied health, reproductive health) documented.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
  - Physical examination findings (cardiorespiratory, abdominal, lymph nodes, skin, neurological).
  - Specific names, doses, routes, and frequencies for current medications (Seroxat, malaria prophylaxis, paracetamol, ibuprofen).
  - Exact malaria prophylaxis regimen and adherence details.
  - Pregnancy status or contraception use; sexual health history.
  - Alcohol quantity/frequency details.
  - Mental health screening details (mood, PHQ-9, suicidal ideation).
  - Basic point-of-care tests (urinalysis, rapid CRP) and documented results.
  - Exact blood tests requested beyond malaria films and inflammatory markers (e.g., FBC, electrolytes, LFTs, malaria PCR).

- Internal contradictions from the transcript:
  - None identified. (Patient uncertain of malaria prophylaxis name and described both "daily" dosing and "another one taken on top of the first" — recorded as patient uncertainty; not a direct contradiction.)

- Comment on transcript quality:
  - Conversation generally intelligible with some brief clarifications required; a few medication specifics and travel exposure details were unclear or not recalled by the patient. Overall adequate for documenting presenting symptoms and immediate plan but lacking objective examination and diagnostic data.
